<!-- pr-reviewer: e15910b3913b01adbf9e01da8e72d7e8478060d9 -->

Reviewed on the cheap tier at the maintainer's instruction. A tool's holder feeds the collision checks, and this PR decides which holder a NEW tool gets, so it is under AGENTS.md's safety floor and its review should run at the high tier; treat this pass as a first screen, not the full verdict. It also adds a dependency between workspace crates (camcraft-post -> camcraft-tools), a maintainer decision.

**Verdict: no blockers found by this screen. Not for merge by this review; a maintainer and a high-tier review should look at it before merge.**

## What looks good
- Trial merge with origin/main (a124496c) was clean; no conflicts.
- Existing tools and the old `AddTool::new` path are unchanged. Tool-library import, project load, undo/redo replay and MCP `"holder":"none"` never call `with_holder` with `MachineDefault` (only `mcp/edit.rs:157` and `ui state.rs` do).
- Validation is by key name at all three doors (`crates/post/src/machine/tooling.rs:59-84`, `parse.rs:209-211`, `validate.rs:117`).
- The reach pin uses the real generate path and reads the cache warnings (`crates/app/tests/machine_default_holder.rs:243-295`).
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the added lines.
- Files stay under 400 lines (parse.rs 390, fields.rs 332; no new file is over).

## Local results (trial merge + origin/main)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `machine_default_holder` | 10 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-post` (all binaries) | all pass, 0 failed |
| app: `holder_library` 11, `machine` 33, `machine_assign` 3, `machine_edit` 12, `machine_key_order` 2, `machine_library` 11, `project_roundtrip` 71, `tool_library` 13, `mcp` 13, `mcp_setup` 6, `mcp_accessory` 1, `mcp_model` 5, `mcp_plate` 1 | all pass |
| ui `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- machines` (CWD crates/ui) | 13 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the batch and release tiers, the `--ignored` lanes, and the full app set; the author's own batch gate covers those.

## Answers to the checklist
1. **No law change.** No verify, collision, reach or motion file changed. `AddTool::new` is unchanged apart from the two new fields set to `None` (`commands/tool.rs:79-82`). Project load: `an_existing_project_loads_unchanged` (passed); the parse and serde fields are `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]` (`def.rs:196-206`), so an old project saves back unchanged.
2. **Visible.** The GUI status line names the holder or the skip (`ui state.rs` AddTool arm). MCP replies with `holder`, `holder_from` and `note` (`mcp/edit.rs:165-170`). The skipped path adds NO holder: `with_holder` sets `skipped` and leaves `holder` as `None` (`commands/tool.rs:94-104`). A tool on a mounted machine with no holder is a bare cylinder as before; the note is shown only at add time, not stored on the tool (the author says so too).
3. **Reach pin.** It drives `GenerateOperation` twice on the same tool and wall and counts `FixtureHit{Holder}` warnings from the cache. Bare: 0; default BT30 ER20: more than 0. Real verify path, not a helper.
4. **Validation.** Each refusal names the key (`tooling.spindle_mount` or `tooling.default_holder`) and the rule. The taper mismatch (`TTS` with `BT30 ER20`) is refused by `matches()` (`tooling.rs:48-54`). Non-string values are refused by `word()` (`tooling.rs:26-32`) with no panic. Unknown extra keys are still tolerated: no `deny_unknown_fields` in the post crate (grep: only `crates/tools/src/catalog_asset.rs`). An older build ignores the keys.
   - Question (not blocking): `default_holder` without `spindle_mount` is allowed and never checked against a mount; `spindle_mount` without a holder is allowed. Both sensible, but please confirm this is the intended reading.
5. **Machine files.** Five spot-checked (770mx, microarc4, pcnc770, 1100m, pcnc1100-s1): valid JSON, keys inside `tooling`, the `mount_source` string present; MX → BT30 / BT30 ER20, M and PCNC → TTS / TTS ER20. The reader resolves the holder ids (the `the_shipped_tormach_mills_state_their_mount` test passed). No Autodesk or HSMWorks citation. PR #807 (a fork draft) touches `crates/app/src/machine/validate.rs`, `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs` and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, the same files this PR edits. The keys are in their own `tooling` block and do not clash textually today, but expect a merge conflict in `validate.rs` and `parse.rs` when the second of the two lands.
6. **Dependency.** `crates/post/Cargo.toml:11` adds `camcraft-tools` as a workspace path dependency. `Cargo.lock` gains only that one edge line (`camcraft-tools` is already in the lock with serde and serde_json only). `camcraft-tools` does not depend on `camcraft-post` directly or through another crate, so there is no cycle. This is a layering decision for the maintainer (AGENTS.md "One concern per subcrate"); it is not mine to approve or block.
7. **MCP and UI.** The `add_tool` schema documents `holder` (`mcp/tools.rs:207`). The PR touches no process file: no `AGENTS.md` root, `.claude/agents`, `.claude/skills`, `xtask`, `.cargo`, or `scripts/gate.*`. The camcraft-mcp skill gap is named in the body. The new editor fields "Spindle mount" and "Default holder" (`machine/fields.rs:199-200`) are fed into the validator's refusal list by key (`validate.rs:117`), so an invalid combination shows its refusal on the field. No UI test names them; a structural AccessKit assertion for the two fields is owed as a follow-up, not a blocker.

## Requested before merge
None found by this screen. The high-tier review is still owed (safety floor), and the crate dependency needs the maintainer's decision.

## Notes
- The body's `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #828` are present; `docs/decisions/828-machine-default-holder.md` is present.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` changed; it is not on the process-file list, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is required for it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e15910b3913b01adbf9e01da8e72d7e8478060d9 -->

**Needs changes before merge.** This is the high-tier review the earlier screen asked for. It found one safety blocker: on every shipped Tormach file, the machine's default holder makes the holder checks *looser* for a new tool, in the band just above the shank. The PR and its decision record both say the opposite. Maintainer question (not blocking): is the new `camcraft-post -> camcraft-tools` edge acceptable? It makes no cycle; details in the notes.

## What looks good
- The design is careful. The default is applied only when a tool is added, inside the add's own undo step (`AddTool::apply`, `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs:141-143`), so one undo removes the tool and its holder. `AddTool::new` (import, replay) is unchanged, and no existing tool is touched.
- One rule is enforced at three doors: the reader, the pane validator and `is_sane` all apply the same `tooling_refusals` (`crates/post/src/machine/tooling.rs`). Each refusal names its key. An unknown holder, a holder off the stated mount, a non-word and an empty value are all refused. Nothing falls back silently to no holder.
- If the default cannot take the tool, the tool is added bare (the behaviour before this PR) and the status line or the MCP `note` says why. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP `add_tool` takes `holder` and replies with `holder`, `holder_from` and `note`; `load_machine` shows both keys. The shared `library_body` keeps `SetToolBody::library` and the add path refusing alike.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in added non-test code. No snapshot PNG changes. A provenance line is on the new module, and a `docs/decisions/828-*.md` entry is present.

## Local results (trial merge with origin/main 9630c86e, clean)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-post lib (incl. 6 new `tooling_tests`) / `mch_head_search` / `post_engine` | 15 / 2 / 33 passed |
| camcraft-tools lib | 54 passed |
| app `machine_default_holder` | 10 passed |
| app `holder_library` 11, `machine` 33, `machine_assign` 3, `machine_edit` 12, `machine_library` 11, `setup_mount` 6, `tool_body` 12, `sim_tool_body` 7, `tool_library` 13, `project_roundtrip` 71, `mcp` 13, `mcp_setup` 6, `commands_undo` 32, `tormach_machines` 6, `golden_cl` 25 | all passed |
| ui `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 525 passed, 1 failed - `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam`, from `main`, not this PR (see notes) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the batch and release tiers, the `--ignored` lanes, and snapshots (release-lane).

## Requested before merge
1. **The default holder narrows the judged envelope in the nut band, so a wall the checks flagged before is no longer flagged.** The catalog's milling tools carry a 44 mm × 35 mm holder cylinder, standing on the shank's top. The default library bodies are narrower there:
   - The ER20 nut is Ø35 × 19.5 mm (`crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:96`), and the body below the flange stays that width.
   - For TTS, the widest part is the Ø38.1 collar (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_tts.rs:29`).

   `HolderProfile::stack` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs:213`) sweeps the body's bands instead of the record's cylinder. `enclose` (`:232-245`) sets `holder_d` to the body's widest, which for TTS is 38.1 < 44. It does not keep the record's value as a floor.

   **Reproduction:** a local-only probe, never pushed. It is a copy of `face_on_770mx` from `crates/app/tests/machine_default_holder.rs` with the wall moved to `xmax + 20.0`, `CUT_Z + 55.0`, height 10. That puts the wall 20 mm off the tool axis, 55-65 mm above the tip: inside the old r22 cylinder, outside the r17.5 nut.
   ```
   PROBE tormach-770mx: bare holder hits = 30, default holder hits = 0
   PROBE tormach-770m:  bare holder hits = 30, default holder hits = 0
   ```
   A user who adds a tool from the catalog on any of the 15 shipped Tormach machines now gets this narrower verdict without choosing it. The decision record says the default "makes the check stricter, visibly" (`docs/decisions/828-machine-default-holder.md`, "Why"). The reach pin's comment says "stricter, never looser" (`machine_default_holder.rs` above `the_default_holder_is_judged_by_the_reach_laws`). The pin tests only the flange side, which is taller than the record's cylinder.

   **Fix, author's choice:**
   - (a) Make the default never looser than what the tool would have been judged with. For example, land the default only when its envelope encloses the record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder, and otherwise add the tool bare with a `note` that says why. Or judge the union of the two.
   - (b) If the maintainer decides the stated holder should win because it is the real holder (it may well be more accurate), say so in the decision record and the test comment instead of "stricter". Pin the narrowing with a test like the probe above, and make the status line or MCP `note` say the holder replaced the record's larger cylinder.

   Either way, the "never looser" claim must match the code.

## Notes (non-blocking)
- **Crate edge (maintainer's call):** `crates/post/Cargo.toml:11` adds `camcraft-tools`, a leaf crate that depends only on serde and serde_json. `sim` and `motion` already depend on it the same way, so there is no cycle and no external dependency. The ui -> app -> flecs layering is untouched. The open question is only "one concern per subcrate": the post crate's machine reader now knows the holder library.
- A project whose stored machine has a `default_holder` that later stops resolving (a library rename, or a file from a newer build) fails to load as a whole. `is_sane` (`crates/post/src/machine/def.rs:244`) would refuse it with "machine definition states a limit that cannot be meant" (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs:572`) or the setup-mount equivalent. That message does not name `tooling.default_holder`, and a default holder is not a limit. Consider naming the key, or dropping a stale default with a note.
- `default_holder` without `spindle_mount` is accepted and never checked against a mount. That is fine for the shipped files, but the earlier screen asked the same question and it still has no answer.
- No structural UI assertion covers the two new editor fields (`crates/app/src/machine/fields.rs:200-201`). The camcraft-mcp skill doc does not mention the `holder` argument; a follow-up is owed.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (4294 lines) grows by 6 lines. It was already over the 400-line target, so this is not blocking.
- The one UI failure is in `main` already:
  ```
  these lines print directly, which a browser drops - use diag_warn!/diag_info!: ["refusal_ghost.rs:44"]
  ```
  `crates/ui/src/refusal_ghost.rs:44` (`eprintln!`, from 90e3be04) meets the diag-seam law from #847. This PR does not touch that file.
- PR #807 touches `validate.rs` and `parse.rs` too; expect a small conflict when the second of the two lands.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The one blocker from the review of e15910b3 (the machine-default holder judging looser than the bare tool) is fixed.

## What looks good
- The previous blocker is closed: an assumed default holder is judged by the union of its bands and the catalog's 44 x 35 mm stand-in cylinder (`HolderProfile::floored`, `crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`, applied in `tool_body::judged`). A holder picked explicitly keeps its real shape. The `machine_default` flag is an additive key on the tool body, so older files read as "explicit" with no version step.
- Design stays tight: the default lands only inside `AddTool::apply` (one undo removes tool and holder); `AddTool::new` and existing tools are untouched; an unbuildable default adds the tool bare with a named note, no silent substitute.
- The `camcraft-post -> camcraft-tools` edge is gone: the holder library is passed in as a lookup by app (`crates/app/src/machine/holders.rs`). `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.
- One rule, three doors (reader, pane validator, stored-machine check), every refusal names its key. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in added non-test code; windows-based indexing in `floored` is safe. No snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG edits, no `build.rs`/`.github`/scripts/dependency changes. Provenance lines present, decision record in `docs/decisions/828-*.md`, body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #828`.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The first ui lib run showed 5 failures in colour-vision/path/preview tests (`law_tests::path_tests::*`, `path_lines::tests::the_mark_follows_the_colour_vision_palette_and_the_dim`, ...) in code this PR does not touch; an immediate re-run passed 527/0. It looks flaky, not caused by the PR.
- A stored machine whose `default_holder` later stops resolving is refused at project load; worth naming the key there if it ever bites.
- The camcraft-mcp skill doc does not yet mention the `holder` argument of `add_tool`; a follow-up is owed.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 7594010a2008df7ca9264775a16e7bc124366255 -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is the high-tier re-review of the fix round (delta e15910b3..7594010a, which includes a merge of origin/main 3bd54fc9). The one blocker from the previous high-tier review is fixed, and both maintainer decisions are carried out. I re-checked only the delta; the parts the first review found sound were not reviewed again.

## What looks good
- **Blocker 1 is closed. A default holder never judges looser than the bare tool.** `HolderProfile::floored` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs:233-253`) takes the union of the body's bands and the stand-in cylinder (`holder_radius` x `holder_len`, standing on the shank's top). It splits at every band edge, and in each slice it keeps the largest radius that covers the slice midpoint. A gap left between the two is filled at the shank radius, as `stack` does. `from_bands` then calls `merge`, which only ever grows a band. I checked the result height by height:
  - **Below the shank top:** the body's own bands are kept.
  - **Inside the 35 mm stand-in:** the radius is max(body, 44/2).
  - **Above the stand-in:** the body's bands are kept.
  - **Holders shorter or taller than the stand-in, and a holder narrow at the bottom and wide above:** all covered by the same construction.

  `bottom()` does not change, so `fits` and `enclose` cannot newly refuse. Indexing is `windows(2)` only, and non-finite input returns the body unchanged.
- **The floor is used where the laws read the holder.** It is applied in `tool_body::judged` (`crates/app/src/tool_body.rs:176`), and every holder law reads through `judged`: generate (`operation/job.rs:139`), `fixture_struck`, the machine checker, `posting_index_swing` and `sim_tool_body`. No law reads `ToolBody::profile()` directly; only the body page and the view preview do.
- **The probe is reproduced end to end.** `an_assumed_default_never_judges_looser_than_the_bare_tool` places a wall 20 mm off the axis, 55-65 mm above the tip, on the 770MX (BT30 ER20) and the 770M (TTS ER20):
  - the bare tool hits the wall;
  - the default holder gets at least as many hits;
  - the same holder picked by name gets 0 hits.

  The tools-crate twin also sweeps 401 heights against both the body and the cylinder.
- **The flag is not lost or flipped by accident:**
  - It is set only on the `MachineDefault` arm of `AddTool` (`commands/tool.rs:107`), inside the add's own undo step. Undo and redo replay the same stored body; this is pinned.
  - `DeleteTool`, `DeleteEntity` and `SetToolBody`'s `prev` all store a full `ToolBody` clone, so undo restores the flag.
  - `EditTool` re-checks the body's fit without rebuilding it. The floor is computed from the current `tool.geom()`, so editing the tool's holder cylinder moves the floor with it.
  - Changing the machine leaves the flag alone (the conservative choice).
  - Save and load carry the flag (`tool_body_wire.rs:68,100,119`). A file without the key reads as explicit, and a lathe body always writes false. Both cases are pinned in `an_assumed_holder_stays_assumed_through_the_file`.
  - The flag only clears when the user sets a body on purpose with `SetToolBody` (file, spun or library). That counts as picking a holder by the maintainer's rule.
- **Stamp.** `tool_body::digest` (called from `operation/stamp.rs:122`) writes a `machine-default` term, so changing the flag invalidates cached toolpaths and verdicts.
- **Decision 2: the dependency is gone.** `crates/post/Cargo.toml` and the merged `Cargo.lock` (the `camcraft-post` entry) no longer list `camcraft-tools`. The library is passed in as `HolderLookup` / `HolderInfo`, and the app's `machine::holders` shadows `parse_mch`, `tooling_refusals` and `tooling_refusal` over the `pub use camcraft_post::machine::*` glob. In app and ui, every direct call into the post crate goes through `parse_mch_with(.., Some(&holder_lookup))`. All four app doors that store a machine pair `is_sane()` with the library-checked `tooling_refusal`: `LoadMachine::new`, `SetSetupMachine::new`, `project/apply.rs:569`, and `mount_dto.rs:44`.
- **Laws:**
  - No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in added non-test code.
  - The project-file key is additive (`serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`), and older files keep their previous behaviour.
  - No golden, snapshot PNG, `CHANGELOG.md` or `RECOMMENDED.md` changes.
  - The decision record no longer says "stricter" and records both maintainer decisions (`docs/decisions/828-machine-default-holder.md:54,80`).
  - Each test lives in the crate that owns the behaviour: the floor in tools, the lookup in post, the doors in app.
  - Touched files are under 400 lines, except `apply.rs` (834) and `schema.rs` (564), which were already over and grow by 3 and 6 lines.

## Local results (trial merge with origin/main 60057449, clean)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-tools` | 56 + 3 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` | lib 16, axis_direction_cli 3, comp 9, comp_plane 3, mch_head_search 2, post_engine 33 - all passed |
| app `machine_default_holder` | 13 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` 71, `commands_undo` 32, `machine` 33, `golden_cl` 25 | all passed |
| app `tool_body_bands` 13, `tool_body_judged` 8, `sim_tool_body` 7, `tool_body` 12, `holder_library` 11, `drilling_cross_holder` 2 | all passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the ui suites, the batch and release tiers, the `--ignored` lanes, and the snapshots (release-lane).

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (non-blocking)
1. **What the author's one stated behaviour change touches.** Since this round, the post crate's own `parse_mch` (no library) keeps an unknown `tooling.default_holder` word instead of refusing it. Its callers are the `post` binary (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs:117`), the inversion re-read (`post/invert.rs:82`) and the safe-retract re-read (`post/machine.rs:372`). None of them applies a holder or feeds a collision check. Every path that lands a holder or stores a machine goes through the app's library-checked reader. Even if one did not, `AddTool`'s default arm would add the tool bare, with a named note, when the holder does not resolve. So this is a note, not a blocker.
2. **Re-picking the default turns the floor off.** If a user opens the holder page and re-picks the same library holder (or changes its gauge), the body becomes explicit and loses the floor. That matches the maintainer's rule (a pick is explicit), but the UI does not tell the user that this happens. A one-line hint on the body page could help later.
3. **The floor is computed on every `judged` call.** It is cheap (at most about 34 bands), so this is only a note.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
